title: Graph API - Docs by LangChain
content:
The graph API is the core of LangGraph. You define a state schema, add nodes that read and update that state, and connect them with edges.

State is normally a TypedDict. Each key has its own reducer function; if no reducer is specified, updates to that key overwrite the previous value. Annotated is used to attach a reducer, for example Annotated[list, add_messages] to append messages rather than replace them.

    from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
    from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

    builder = StateGraph(State)
    builder.add_node("my_node", my_node)
    builder.add_edge(START, "my_node")
    builder.add_conditional_edges("my_node", router)
    graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())

Nodes are plain functions that accept the state and return a partial update. Conditional edges route to a next node based on a function of the state. You must compile the graph before invoking it. Supplying a checkpointer makes execution durable and is required for interrupts and for resuming a paused run.

title: Everything You Need To Know About Azure AI Search In 2026
content:
In this article I will explain everything about Azure AI Search agentic retrieval based on my own experiments. Note that some details here may be out of date and I have simplified several concepts. Agentic retrieval basically splits your question into smaller questions and searches for each one. I found it worked well but the pricing was confusing.
